subject.title: Reconcile externally managed channels by provider identity

question: Should ClickClack core own a provider-neutral, persistent reconciliation API for externally managed channels, or should integrations continue composing the existing channel operations?
rationale: The proposal adds a new durable identity model, endpoint, SDK surface, and immutability contract; source-level implementation can follow either direction, but choosing the permanent core boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core reconcile API
options.body: Adopt the provider-scoped identity and atomic endpoint as a deliberately versioned managed-channel capability, with migration and concurrency guarantees.

options.title: Keep composition outside core
options.body: Retain the current managed-channel primitives and ask integrations to handle identity and deduplication in their own storage or workflow layer.

options.title: Defer the contract decision
options.body: Leave the issue open without implementation until a concrete integration demonstrates that the existing primitives cannot meet its operational requirements.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core reconcile API
recommendation.body: Adopt the provider-scoped identity and atomic endpoint as a deliberately versioned managed-channel capability, with migration and concurrency guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged managed-channel foundation is the directly adjacent product and implementation surface.
